modelVerification: explicit invocation only; CLI did not echo model

findings.message: Record lastCheckpointGC only after successful cleanup. Updating it before GC, together with removing GC's error return, suppresses retries after listing or deletion failures until checkpointsGCInterval elapses (10 minutes by default). Restore error propagation and update the timestamp only on success.
findings.evidence: recommender.go:158-160 updates the timestamp unconditionally before calling GC. cluster_feeder.go:294-310 logs listing errors and returns; lines 323-325 log deletion errors and continue without reporting failure. Subsequent maintenance calls use the updated timestamp to decide whether GC is due.

findings.message: Start GC's timeout independently after checkpoint writing finishes. The single deadline now covers both sequential operations, so writing can consume GC's entire budget and GC then receives an expired context. Restore separate write and GC contexts derived from the parent.
findings.evidence: RunOnce creates stepCtx at recommender.go:190-192. MaintainCheckpoints passes that same context first to StoreCheckpoints at line 156 and then to GC at line 160. checkpoint_writer.go:115-118 checks cancellation after processing each VPA and line 134 waits for workers, allowing writing to return after the deadline. cluster_feeder.go:323 passes the inherited context directly to checkpoint deletion. Previously, CHANGE.diff shows GC's timeout started after StoreCheckpoints returned.

result.coverage: Reviewed TASK.json, CHANGE.diff, all four changed production files, and checkpoint_writer.go. Traced configuration defaults, controller construction and loop, maintenance sequencing, writer cancellation, and GC failure paths. Kept the two contract violations separate; did not report the equivalent write-deadline expression as an independent defect.
limitations: External client and lister implementations are unavailable; deletion behavior with an expired context was not executed.
No deployment configuration or external callers were supplied, so compatibility consequences of removing the GC timeout flag were not established.
result.contribution: Established from staged source that GC failures advance the scheduling timestamp and that writer cancellation can leave GC with an already-expired context. Limited findings to retry scheduling and timeout isolation without claiming observed downstream failures.
